body: One of 16 most sacred Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka. It is believed that the lord Buddha visited this place to resolve a conflict between two rulers of the island. The monks of this temple had gone through immense of hardships to protect this place during the civil war. In the temple museum you can find lot of information regarding this. Since it is located in a small island separated from the main land it has an added additional value. You need to take a boat from the kurikadduwan jetty to reach here. Boats operate regularly and it take about 20 mins for the ride. Ticket is 40 rupees one way. They load a lot of people per boat, so don’t expect any comfort. Boat will drop you at the temple jetty. But to take the return boat you need to walk or take a tuk towards the jetty near the Hindu kovil which is about 1km away.

body: Nagadeepa Purana Vihara is an ancient Buddhist temple situated in Jaffna district of Northern Province, Sri Lanka. It is among the country's sixteen holiest Buddhist shrines.The Nagadeepa Viharaya is one of the 16 most sacred places of worship in Sri Lanka. According to the chronicles, in the 5th year after enlightenment, the Lord Buddha visited Nagadeepa to settle a dispute between two Naga Kings - Chulodara and Mahodara, regarding the possession of a gem studded throne. The Bak Maha Amawaka Poya Day commemorates the Lord Buddha's visit to Nagadeepa.
title: Nagadeepa Viharaya is one of the 16 most sacred places of worship in Sri Lanka

body: The temple is located in the island of Nainativu ,which is situated in about 35 km from Jaffna city centre.You need to travel by a vehicle upto the island of Pungudutivu,which is about 1.5 hour drive.Once you reach the end of Punkudathiv island drive way,you have to travel by boat for about 20 minutes to reach the Nainativu island.The boats(so called ''FERRY'S") are outdated fishing boats which are NOT entirely SAFE for passenger transport.Yo have to get in a line to get n the boats.They provide life jackets which are of poor quality.They loades about 40 people to a single boat,which has very poor ventilation and limited space.Plus the noise of the motor is so loud that you cannot even talk among others.We somehow reached the Nagadeepa viharaya,which s the first stop, but it was difficult to get out from the boat as most people were travelling beyond that stop.There was no one to tell us to get off that stop and there was poor guidance from boat staff.Once you worship the viharaya,you have to reach to the other end of the island to catch a returning boat.It is difficult to walk in heating sun specially if you are have young kids.There are few three wheelers available,which can be hired for Rs,100/=.We were so afraid to travel back in a same kind of boat,which was loading so many passengers at the time we reached the pier.With the help of a Navy officer at the pier,we managed to hire a single boat for RS.2500/= and came back to island with out much damage.But those boats are also in same bad condition as the previous one,but the plus point is that ,there was only four of us in the boat so we could at least breathe properly.I think the transport should be improved for the sake of everybody,the tourists and the villagers!!

body: Our driver from the Valampuei Hotel parked at the Parking lot and we walked along the causeway to the Ferry section. We got into a privately owned Ferry. Getting in and out is tough for the elderly and less agile. You sit in the bowels of the boat as it were and take off, to the Nagadipa Island. Our driver mentioned that the sea is 250 meters deep in some sections, and I certainly prayed that we wouldn't have to find that out for ourseves ! ! The life jackets we are requested to wear aren't exactly sea worthy ! ! The fare is less than moderate. Rs.30/- per head for the ride. The temple is ancient but all traces of it have vanished in modernization. The older viharage still stands. The surrounds are kept clean. Voluntary donations are being collected for a massive Buddha statue and Edifice to be built at the entrance way. ( How much it will enhance the place or take away from it, is up for conjecture) The priest speaks Tamil very fluently. Most villagers passing by were stopped and spoken to thus. The downside for me was a starving dying puppy dog. Lying in the scorching sun. I bought some milk but it was too far gone to accept any, although I tried ! The positive was that its' equally starved brother or sister lapped up the milk greedily. We need more Metta and Karuna here, as we do everywhere else.

body: I was told it's a 20 minute ferry ride to the island. It is also nearly an hours drive from Jaffna along the bumpy causeway road! body: This site is at immense significance to Sri Lankan Buddhists. Despite the significance the temple itself was small and simple yet full of tranquility.The biggest downside though was a completely unsafe sea journey. Life jackets were given to everyone but nearly all of those were way past use by date and worn out and broken. The on-boarding and off-boarding was challenging to elderly especially women. This is an important point given large number of elderly visiting the site given it was inaccessible for 30 years due to the war. The ferry tend to be overcrowded and I wondered if it was even sea worthy. The fare was extremely reasonable Rs 30 though. I am sure people are willing to pay a lot more for safety and accessibility. Part of the blame goes to the Navy who is 'supervising' the operation. The other half goes to whoever the authority letting these shonky operators to continue.In addition the road from Jaffna to Nagadeepa wasn't at best condition. Some sections were excellent but there is lot more work to be done.
title: Unsafe sea journey

body: I am a Sri Lankan Buddhist who visited Nagadeepa for the first time in my life last December. I was part of a group of 19 people - a pregnant woman; 4 senior citizens; a woman with a chronic back problem and 7 children.We were advised to be at the ferry point sharp at 8.00 am presumably to get into the best ferry to make the 20 minute journey to Nagadeepa from Karainagar. However, we missed the 8.00 am mark by a few minutes and were lined up in a hallway to take the next ferry.Here are my observations:1) The ferry terminal and ferries are supervised by the Sri Lanka Navy2) One wall of the hall has pictorial instructions to wear the life jacket but most of it is faded3) Ferries are like Dhows that are used by Omani's. People are forced into the larger lower level but that is a few feet above water - scary to sit in a dingy environment with no room to escape if the boat were to take in water4) Life jackets are worn out and not tested to be sea worthy. Those with zippers are cannot be closed due to broken zippers; those with interlocking straps cannot be used as plastic locks are broken5) Observed a Navy personnel (he stated his rank as Leading Seaman) asking the ferry operator the reason for getting a lesser number of people. The ferry was actually crawling since I knew that there were more than the recommended number of people in that boat - seems to be the SL Navy personnel working "hand in glove" with ferry operators and not worrying about the safety of the people taking those ferriesFinally, as a Buddhist, I did not find any significance at Nagadeepa. It does not have the same reckoning as the Gangaramaya temple in Colombo. I wasted half day of valuable time of my Jaffna tour by going to Nagadeepa.
title: A disaster - not worth the risk and the time!

body: It is believed as one of the three places which Lord Gautama Buddha has visited Sri Lanka. Apart from that there's a Hindu Kovil in this Nainathiv island. If you want to go by public transport, there is a bus service from Jaffna bus stand. The route is Jaffna - Kuraikattuwan. It runs through an island called Punkuduthiv. Kuraikattuwan is the jetty of Punkuduthiv island. From there, a boat service is operated. Usually all passengers should where life jackets, but the quality of them are not good at all. Nowadays Sri Lanka Navy is controlling the number of passengers per boat. Safety is therefore not a problem.The temple doesn't have any ancient buildings. All are newly built. However the history goes back to 2600 years ago. It is historic for the famous "Chulodara - Mahodara" war which has been settled by Lord Buddha. It is one of the evidence of early settlements and civilizations in Sri Lanka. For non-buddhists it may be just a trip because there's nothing interesting to see around there. But the boat trip and the bus ride is a quite different feeling.
title: Must visit site for Buddhists

body: Trip to Nagadipa Temple is like an adventure. The route from Jaffna runs askew along causeway to the Kayts and another cause way to the Punkudativu. body: According the Buddhist history Lord Buddha visited Nagadeepa to settle a dispute between two "Naga" kings during the second visit to Sri Lanka. It's one of the sixteen holiest Buddhist shrines. From there you'll have to take a boat to Nagadeepa. The boats are modified fishing boats and the experience in them is not so good unless you could sit on one of the four ladders that provides entry to the hull which provides a good outside view. Road Development Authority also operates few boats which are quite good with nice seating positions to look outside. Boats will drop you to the jetty which directly leads to the temple. If you are just a tourist don't expect much unless you appreciate being in such environment because it's a place of worship. There you have the stupa (said to contain the throne which started the dispute between the Naga kings), image house, museum, sacred Bo tree, sacred Kiripalu tree (said to be carried out all the way from India by a deity named "Samiddhi Sumana" who came along with Lord Buddha), statue of Lord Buddha and a replica of the throne enshrined in the stupa.Best times to visit will be the early mornings because it gets very hot during mid day. The boat service starts from 7.00 am. Tuk tuks are available on the island if you want to go site seeing.

body: Nagadeepa Purana Vihara is located on the island of "Nainativu" and one among the cluster of islands located off the Jaffna peninsula and located around 35 kilometres away from the Jaffna town. It is believed that Lord Buddha has once stepped in this island and hence is one of the most sacred places for Buddhists. To get there, you can drive or ride on your own or use public transport-as there are buses plying up and down from Jaffna to "Kurikadduwan"- which is the jetty for Nainativu. The ferry to Nainativu starts here and will take only 15~20 minutes for the journey but you will have to stay in the queue for about 45 minutes or even 1 hour during the weekend or on Sri Lankan holidays. The ferry boats used are not in their best shape; you may even have to take your ride on top of the boat. To get in, you will have to jump in while it keeps bobbing up and down in the choppy water. When you land on the island, there is a long paved walk which will take you to the shrine. Once you have completed the tour, make sure to go to the museum, which contain many artefacts related to the history of the temple and other rare exhibits. After visiting the temple, you have to take a short walk towards "Naga Pooshani Amban Kovil" and get on to the ferry for the return journey from the pier outside the Kovil. If you happen to spend sometime in the Jaffna peninsula, make sure you include a visit to Nagadeepa in your itinerary.
title: A sacred island

body: Located with approx: 45 minutes drive from Jaffna town. The boat service is conducted by the Sri Lanka army. It takes about 15 minutes on the boat to go to Nagadeepa from the Jetty. History connected to NagadeepaNagadeepa Purana Viharaya is an ancient Buddhist temple situated in Jaffna district of Northern Province, Sri Lanka. It is among the country's sixteen or seventeen holiest Buddhist shrines (Solosmasthana). According to contemporary history, the Gautama Buddha visited the site after five years of attaining Enlightenment to settle the dispute between two warring Naga kings, Chulodara and Mahodara.Ancient history according to the Mahavamsa chronicles and the Tamil Buddhist epic Manimekalai mentions a gem-studded throne and a stone with the Buddha’s footprint at the island Nainativu, (also known as Nagadeepa) which pilgrims from India visited.The site is known as the place where Lord Buddha came during his second visit to Sri Lanka, after five years of attaining Enlightenment, to intervene and mediate in settling a dispute over the possession of a gem-studded throne.When Buddha arrived and saw the Naga Kings prepared for fighting, Budhha used psychic powers to appear in the sky performing miracles. This made the Nagas astonished and happy. After having listened to the Dhamma sermons displaying Buddha's masterly knowledge of unity and harmony, meththa and compassion, the Naga kings paid homage to Budhha with overwhelming faith. The throne was offered to him in unison and they became pious devotees.The Naga King Maniakkitha, ruler of Kelaniya, moved by the compassion of the Buddha, thanked him profusely for settling the dispute.He further pleaded for a souvenir to worship and consequently the Buddha offered him the Kiripalu tree and the throne. A deity named Samiddhi Sumana, who had made the banyan tree his abode, accompanied him to Thathagatha while in Jetavanarama, holding the uprooted tree as an umbrella to him.According to the golden Sannasa Wallipuram, committed to writing during the reign of king Vasabha, the temple was reconstructed by pious kings including Devanampiyatissa and Dutugemunu and converted into a sacred place.
title: Nagadeepa

body: Buddhist Temple and the grand Naga Pooshani Amman Kovil of the North Sri Lanka ... The temple can be reached from Jaffna city with initial road travel upto KKD ie KURIKADDUVAN (Last Stop ), & from there an approx 20/25 minutes ferry trip to the island of NAINATIVU. The initial road travel (Approx 1 hour and 25 minutes) too is an unique and awesome experience, since it passes over the narrow causeway, beware that during my visit (Jan 2014), I found the road to be in very bad condition than the ones in rest of Sri Lanka. All along the causeway you will find large number of fishing nets, as the travel progresses their is a very beautiful Kovil along the road on the right hand side. Once reaching the last stop, you will be hopping into a ferry along with other people, in the presence of the Smiling and cooperative SL Navy officers presence. The ferry reaches the jetty which leads to the historically significant Buddhist Temple,. The temple is recently renovated and some work was still in progress.. After the Temple visit, move on to the grand and beautifully decorated and painted NAGA POOSHANI AMMAN KOVIL Lovely experience alltogeather!!Ahhhh.... well..... before I forget ... one small advice would be to combine the Delft island visit and the Nainativu island visit.... You have to be there on the KKD departure jetty on some MONDAY, THURSDAY OR FRIDAY, before 0900AM, catch the ferry trip to Delft island and return back from their by the 1400 Hrs boat, back to KKD departure jetty and then hop in the ferry trip to Nainativu... Because Ferry for Delft island is very limited at this time... for Nainativu island visit there is a ferry at interval of every 20-25 minutes .
title: Buddhist Temple and the grand Naga Pooshani Amman Kovil of the North Sri Lanka ...

body: The boat is full with inhabitnats of the Naintivu island. It is a good experience to mix with locals. THe Buddhist temple is adjacent to the Hindu Kovil. Treating both is a way to develop the long lost harmony.

body: We went on a navy boat, so we were not cramped in a hull. The boat rose takes about 15 mins. Looks like just another temple... But there is a historic significance. Better take a walk towards the kovil, because that way you can have a better look at the residents of this island.
title: a temple on an island

body: We went on a tour bus followed by a ferry crossing to the island.The journey across the little causeways lined by prawns and crab traps in the Indian Ocean was just magnificent. The ferry is equipped with life jackets but many do not clip tight and wet and not too clean. However it is only a short journey. Upon arrival it is a beautiful walk to the temple and it is quite historic as apparently Lord Buddha set foot here as well.
title: Beautiful journey

body: The trip to the Temple from Jaffna town, is worth the time invested, The drive to the Ferry over the bridges and prawn farms, is picturesque, it depicts the true nature of the area; we didn't hire a private boat, we went by Ferry it was overcrowded with Locals,we enjoyed it, it wasn't unpleasant, just like any city at peak time.
title: Enjoyable Ferry Crossing

body: This Hindu temple is interesting by itself and worth a visit. It's large and it was interesting to attend the puja. (note that men need to remove the shirt before entering the inside). Even more important, given its distance from Jaffna, it's a reason for a nice day tour to the islands near Jaffna.We hired a car for the day. After driving for an hour or so we reach the water front where you need a short (15-20 minutes) boat ride to the temple. Nearby is a Buddhist temple which also worth a visit.
title: Interesting temple and nice day tour from Jaffna

body: To get to this temple requires a very pleasant drive over multiple causeways to the islands of Kayts, Punkudutivu and then to Kurikadduwam where you then embark on a 15-20 minute (USD) 30c/each way boat trip over to the island of Nainativu. The ferry is an old wooden enclosed boat which is so much fun with the locals, but if you get claustrophobic stick close to the stairwell - we managed to sit at the top of the stairs both ways and it was magnificent (you are not allowed to sit on the roof) the water is smooth and turquoise. Once arriving at Nainativu, you disembark and walk down the long jetty to arrive at Nagadipa Vihara Stupa on the left, and to the right, the walk along the shoreline road dotted with market stalls selling all kinds of interesting fare including huge chunks of Jaggery, temple braids, jewellery and trinkets. There was even a peddlar of good ole fashioned fairy floss in paper cones. The temple itself is extraordinarily colourful and well maintained and loved. The atmosphere was extremely vibrant and everyone seemed in good spirits. Photos are not allowed to be taken inside this temple but the atmosphere is worth going in for. The ferry departs from this temple so there is no need to walk back to the arrival jetty. This was a very enjoyable day engaging with the locals and not to be missed if you are up north. Unfortunately, there wasnt really anywhere to swim. Fresh Mangos, limes, coconuts, water and fruit juice can be purchased at the ferry terminal. Take plenty of water - its hot and you will need to keep hydratedDress Code:Its HOT, so a wide brimmed hat is preferable to a cap. Purchase at the market stalls where you catch the ferry for a couple of dollars (few hundred rupees)Carry a sarong & scarf (to cover shoulders) as there is a dress code in the temple and to protect from the sun,Thongs/ slip ons for ease of taking shoes on and off and to save your feet from the hot sand
title: Magnificent Temple & the journey there is half the fun!

body: Journey to the temple is very memorable! There is a 15 min ferry travel through the Polk Straight.However the ferries are overloaded. Had a long waiting time for the ferry. Temple had a very peaceful atmosphere. However no basic sanitory facilities are available.
title: A Must see!

body: Even though from the jetty point it seems like an interesting idea of a temple situated on an island, the best of this attraction remains the boat ride (15 mins, costs Lankan Rs 30 ) and the approach to the temple itself. Once there, the temple has little to offer to the visitors, even though it may be religiously significant to the pious. The best view is the conical staggered roof of the temple from the arrival walkway or from the main land, but the temple itself is "just another temple".. too colorful and gaudy! Men have to remove their shirt when entering this temple.
title: Best seen from far away

body: This Buddhist temple is quite different to the Nallur Kandswamy temple in Jaffna. The boat trip to the island is an experience itself, and is lovely. The walk from the jetty to the temple is quite enjoyable and pictureseque. The temple itself is serene, calm and a far cry from the hustle, bustle and bright psychedelic colours of the Hindu temples in the area.
title: Calm, serene environment and great boat ride

body: The boat ride was horrid if you have contacts with the Sri Lankan Navy my advice is to get arrange one of their boats. temple is very sacred. though I missed the podi bodhiya it is another sacred place in the island
title: most sacred place

body: traveled with srilanka navy... was a good experience travaling in a navy boat and from nagadeepa temple to nagadeepa kovil we took a dimo batta was a facinating ride
title: memorable

body: The ferry's did not have life jackets , except the navy boats where life jackets were provided. The entrance to the temple has been done up very well is is looking very nice.
title: Visit to Nagadeepa

body: Must visit this beautiful island in Jaffna peninsula. The temple is surrounded by the sea and must visit by the boat, The walking towards the temple from the boat was fantastic. Any one could not ask for more. Ideal location for a temple. Must pay a visit. You feel very peaceful once you are near the Bo tree.
title: Historic temple worth visiting

body: The most beautiful surrounditngs a temple could have. The sea around the temple is spetacular. The time i visited there the toilets had only salt water from tap lines connected from the sea itself. But it wont take so long to pay a visit to this temple so that would not be necessary.
title: Temple in the middle of the sea - Nagadeepa

body: You have to go in Boat to this small island. There we find a Buddhist Temple, a Hindu Temple and a Muslim Mosque. The Muslim Mosque is little far (5 Km) from other two temples.
title: Three Religious Places in one small Island
Peaceful and Religious
body: Nagadeepa Purana Rajamaha vihara is a peaceful and religious place where you can pay homage to lord Buddha and learn about the ancient visit of Lord Buddha to this location. Can reach from Kurikadduwan pier at Pungudutivu island by ferry/Navy boat.

title: Historic
body: The vihara is a must see site on a visit to Jaffna. The boat ride is an adventure in itself and the faint hearted may need a bit of reassurance.

title: Discover more on these island ???
body: A relatively easy to visit from Jaffna by bus which can be taken from the main bus stands The journey will take around 1.5 hours to Punkudutivu cost you RS 75/- from where SL naval junks will take you across for 30Rp (15min). The journey is amazing as you cost along low slung causeways hovering above blue azure waters. Boats leave you on the jetty next to Naga Pooshani Ambal Kovil . After lokking around you walk down the road to left from the jetty to the Buddhist Temple (Nagadipa Vihara) which is being renovated . Boats leave on an hourly basis from a jetty adjacent to Naga Kovil. Once back on Punkudutiva buses back to Jaffna will meet you at the jetty. Easy!There was one more ancient budda temple in the same island it was 400 m from the navy head quarters there are direction board will leads to the temple and the local people was been said that the budda came to these place only . there are some ancient buildings came been seen here should spend little more time to visit these tuk tuk will cost you RS100 to visit and RS100 to get back to jetty

title: Festival July
body: This was a breath taking experience. This temple is truly beautiful and definitely a place to visit if you go to Jaffna. We were lucky to have been apart of the festival held on the day we went there. There was over 20,000 people when we arrived but we were never kept waiting in line for the boat ride. Its about an hours drive from Jaffna town and then a 20min boat ride to the temple. The whole experience was overwhelming. The colours and architecture was what I focused on the most.

title: Journey better than destination
body: You will need an entire morning or afternoon to do this. Involves travel across three smaller islands and a boat ride to get to. Will get a feel for the aftermath of the war on your visit.
